query: For lightweight high-entropy alloys intended for weight-sensitive aerospace and rail-transportation applications, what single, testable intervention hypothesis could improve mechanical performance, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance while retaining low density? Specify the intervention, the proposed causal mechanism, the predicted outcomes relative to an unmodified lightweight-high-entropy-alloy baseline, the conditions under which the hypothesis should hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and a controlled experiment with clear results that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of refractory elements, such as W, Mo, Ta, or Nb, into a lightweight high-entropy alloy system, combined with a suitable processing technique, such as selective laser melting or laser powder bed fusion, can improve mechanical performance, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance while retaining low density.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast or as-printed lightweight high-entropy alloy
generation.intervention: Introduction of refractory elements and suitable processing technique
generation.conditions: High-temperature oxidation resistance, corrosion resistance, and mechanical performance testing
generation.structural_mediator: Grain refinement and formation of a single BCC solid solution
generation.mechanism: The introduction of refractory elements can lead to the formation of a single BCC solid solution, which can improve mechanical performance and corrosion resistance. The suitable processing technique can help to refine the grain structure, further improving the properties. The refractory elements can also help to improve high-temperature oxidation resistance by forming a protective oxide layer.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved mechanical performance, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance while retaining low density
generation.baseline: As-cast or as-printed lightweight high-entropy alloy without refractory elements
generation.boundary: Limitations of the processing technique and potential effects of refractory elements on density
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in the exact composition and processing parameters required to achieve optimal properties

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of mechanical performance, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance between lightweight high-entropy alloys with and without refractory elements, processed using different techniques
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of refractory elements and suitable processing technique does not lead to improved mechanical performance, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance while retaining low density, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Abstract High-entropy alloys (HEAs) exhibit excellent properties such as high strength, good ductility, superior corrosion resistance, and thermal stability, making them highly promising for applications in the aerospace, energy, and automotive industries. Among them, the FeNiCrMn HEA demonstrates outstanding corrosion resistance while eliminating the expensive Co element present in the “Cantor” alloy, significantly reducing costs. However, current research on the FeNiCrMn HEA has primarily focused on its corrosion resistance, with relatively limited studies on its mechanical properties. This paper investigated the effects of different crystal orientations, temperatures, and strain rates on the mechanical properties and plastic deformation mechanisms of an equiatomic FeNiCrMn HEA using molecular dynamics simulations. The results revealed that the FeNiCrMn HEA exhibited significant anisotropy under loading along different orientations, with the maximum yield stress observed along the <11-1> direction. Refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) have excellent mechanical properties, which could make them the substitutes of some superalloys. However, the high melting point of refractory HEAs leads to processing problems when using traditional processing techniques. In this study, a single BCC solid solution of NbMoTaW alloy was formed by selective laser melting (SLM) with a linear energy density of up to 2.83 J/mm. The composition distribution was analyzed, and the element with a lower melting point and lower density showed a negative deviation (no more than 5%) of the molar ratio in the formed alloy. The HEA shows an excellent microstructure, microhardness, and corrosion resistance performance compared with traditional superalloys, making it a new substitute metal with great application prospects in aerospace and energy fields.

Abstract A novel metal matrix composite based on the NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy (HEA) was designed by the in-situ formation method. The microstructure, phase evolution, and compression mechanical properties at room temperature of the composite are investigated in detail. The results confirmed that the composite was primarily composed of body-centered cubic solid solution with a small amount of titanium carbides and alumina. With the presence of approximately 7.0 vol. % Al 2 O 3 and 32.2 vol. % TiC reinforced particles, the compressive fracture strength of the composite (1542 MPa) was increased by approximately 50% compared with that of the as-cast NbMoCrTiAl HEA. In consideration of the superior oxidation resistance, the P/M NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy composite could be considered as a promising high temperature structural material. Keywords: high entropy alloys, metal matrix composites, mechanical properties
